steps.why: Git and less as a session installs them; sixty commits of a file that grows by a line in each and three hundred lines: more than a screen of log, of diff and of page.
steps.script: amy install git > /dev/null && amy install less > /dev/null && git config --global user.name Dolly && git config --global user.email dolly@example.invalid

steps.why: The package's Git commits without a word: it holds the system configuration.
steps.script: for n in $(seq 101 160); do seq 1 $n > file && git add file && git commit -qm change-$n; done 2> /tmp/said && test ! -s /tmp/said

steps.why: Nothing in the environment asks for a pager.
Output that is not a terminal is not paged and never waits for a key, as in a tool call.
steps.script: test "$(git log | grep -c change-)" = 60 && git show > /tmp/shown && grep -q change-160 /tmp/shown
man lines | cmp - /tmp/lines && man lines > /tmp/page && cmp /tmp/page /tmp/lines
